This pattern suggests an intrinsic pathway defect — e.g., factor VIII, IX, XI, or XII deficiency, or presence of an inhibitor (e.g., lupus anticoagulant or acquired factor VIII inhibitor). However, the clinical presentation (mucocutaneous bleeding, easy bruising, post-dental bleeding) is atypical for hemophilia A/B (which usually presents with hemarthroses/muscle bleeds, not isolated mucosal bleeding) — unless mild/moderate deficiency. Factor XI deficiency, in contrast, *does* commonly present with mucosal and post-surgical bleeding — especially after dental or tonsil procedures — and can have near-normal baseline aPTT that prolongs significantly with pre-analytical variables (e.g., delayed processing). Given this, the next most informative test is **factor VIII activity** and **factor XI activity**, but I must request only one per turn.
